Here's a compact digest of new or updated IETF drafts, W3C proposals, or standards-body activity on AI agent authentication, web bot auth, and agent identity from the last 30 days (July 31, 2026, to August 30, 2026):

1.  **IETF `web-bot-auth` Protocol Draft Revised with Standards Track Intent**
    The IETF `web-bot-auth` protocol draft, co-authored by Cloudflare and Google, was revised in August 2026 to include Standards Track intent and absorbed the key-directory draft. This protocol aims to establish cryptographic bot identity using HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421), offering a more reliable alternative to traditional IP allowlists and user-agent strings.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQE_XhOby8dghvAYzZK6UKppfeSKC-pjvl-SSgpkSDtqGSyZow_tqjSF9IGDnT-gIsQ5CwiccVlUau_ObUabvd0x3OIdcs4AFXfW5TTAf7h99YekI6v5Vb9P8wig1JgcayfahD8SWGL8xw==

2.  **IETF Draft Outlines Architectural Requirements for AI Agents on the Internet**
    The `draft-daniel-ai-agent-internet-architecture-00` document, submitted on August 14, 2026, describes architectural requirements for supporting AI agents across various internet protocols. It advocates for profiling and extending existing protocols rather than creating new monolithic ones, covering aspects like authentication, authorization, and agent identity.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGdyQoDUq2Gq0iEAwTzUsHBNotV1aSFurwYGT817xpA6JXop2nhKjDvalUYbE0Q3koCcgsx53ylXmihrfvr5Narg1Gu-85KiNZ4rqJ8ACBSGJiH3lHMoyJTLK1sHHgjPuCaIkAJ558L4M4hpDg-vLnROLvYOhEjhRogHI0quOQZg7ZpM_qV2rw==

3.  **IETF `draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-02` Updated**
    The IETF draft `draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-02`, which defines HTTP Message Signatures for automated traffic, was updated on August 18, 2026. This document is a part of the `webbotauth` working group's ongoing efforts to standardize cryptographic authentication for automated clients.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFJj4eW2FWjq_F3ZcBDof65GJ1MFHodRVzFZ9p_UGYj4wL5tRMYO226ZJ_ROKxuFAwWMwaXIIIfqWLc41KBHz0uSFJWcdrQ0m0b4SUuZDIJjid7I0Xa9_n99OD7Ilf2yIO5WMIJxA==

4.  **New IETF Draft: AI Agent Identity Certificate (AIC) Extension for X.509 v3**
    The `draft-wei-aic-identity-cert-00` proposes an AI Agent Identity Certificate (AIC) Extension for X.509 v3. This extensive 229-page draft, submitted on August 19, 2026, is a foundational piece for binding AI agent cryptographic identity to a responsible principal.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGWAWGiyNl3vECmj_Acv7TGI1KZEpZqfhGyHhauauSt5T0oJtS4Y7dBSXL5ki5NQMX2YEsKcA-ft4cwKtwCqewFpWIGS40DjeMs1TGWMlns0Vd0ajspRzDBOTB5LnvOsX8LWOmIhUOi_3LTrUY7TLI_sXVG48omY_MyQcnUG2XIh_s868bdjPqpMSwozWvOL29CzdWN

5.  **New IETF Draft: Agent Identity Protocol (AIP) for Verifiable Delegation**
    The `draft-prakash-aip-01` introduces an Agent Identity Protocol (AIP) focused on verifiable delegation for AI Agent Systems. This 38-page draft was submitted to the IETF on August 19, 2026.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGWAWGiyNl3vECmj_Acv7TGI1KZEpZqfhGyHhauauSt5T0oJtS4Y7dBSXL5ki5NQMX2YEsKcA-ft4cwKtwCqewFpWIGS40DjeMs1TGWMlns0Vd0ajspRzDBOTB5LnvOsX8LWOmIhUOi_3LTrUY7TLI_sXVG48omY_MyQcnUG2XIh_s868bdjPqpMSwozWvOL29CzdWN

6.  **New IETF Draft: AI Agent Identity Certificate (AIC) JSON Web Token Profile**
    The `draft-wei-aic-jwt-00` defines the JSON Web Token (JWT) profile of the AI Agent Identity Certificate (AIC), complementing `draft-wei-aic-identity-cert-00`. Submitted on August 25, 2026, it aims to enable application-layer authorization semantics for AI agents where transport-layer certificates are unavailable.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGkC4VNPnrkFu0rv_3XiMNGYt4GNAaU5PortxTpazPZ_V4114fts-l4DvD3ILkjas_Sz9-brD66Q0S1JeCjjfPZEJKV67_L00FNv-cZBdybMCzGT7pmetCigBofMYy9vUkLdlcJmcAEOgcipVWA

7.  **IETF Draft Outlines Agentic AI Use Cases and Protocol Requirements**
    The `draft-agentic-ai-usecases-requirements-02` document, updated on August 26, 2026, describes use cases for agentic AI communication systems and derives protocol requirements. It focuses on aspects like agent identity, authentication, authorization, and delegation chains, emphasizing verifiable credentials and revocation mechanisms.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEFWTgGCJD4f9WgSdSmT8KoJuUfcR7SU13pyz0MxkVk46YItnHfUYCxZANLzn4XizPaiAh0PhrIs44mqrObPprw1v0Ey5LcR85sI_j7XIp4ZGpTEC5dj2Wy6SaLNU4Np-uhhs9NrZFHetraco-cdUN_zjeR7wtnQcmMor3G5IHrgyEjwN42sEntXg==

8.  **New IETF Draft: Agent Identity Framework for Autonomous AI Agents**
    The `draft-sharif-agent-identity-framework-01` proposes a framework for trust and identity for autonomous AI agents. This 18-page document was submitted to the IETF on August 27, 2026.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGJkGh3vTH0FOIPSOMJ9RSKvKx0op1Zl8K39pnijNpcuO-eatDNTIADOj2KKtPEp1cVfTsDUStKEQroGFx06_Kpj0WS9X68cJ3MnznqCl7xEwxz-yDeLiyCGYFhbxAer9-N

9.  **New IETF Draft: Trust Scoring and Identity Verification for AI Agent Payment Transactions**
    The `draft-sharif-agent-payment-trust-01` focuses on trust scoring and identity verification specifically for autonomous AI agent payment transactions. This 36-page draft was submitted to the IETF on August 27, 2026.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGJkGh3vTH0FOIPSOMJ9RSKvKx0op1Zl8K39pnijNpcuO-eatDNTIADOj2KKtPEp1cVfTsDUStKEQroGFx06_Kpj0WS9X68cJ3MnznqCl7xEwxz-yDeLiyCGYFhbxAer9-N

10. **New IETF Draft: OpenID Connect Agent Identity Claims for AI Agents**
    The `draft-sharif-openid-agent-identity-01` proposes OpenID Connect Agent Identity Claims for autonomous AI Agents. This 31-page draft was submitted to the IETF on August 27, 2026.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGJkGh3vTH0FOIPSOMJ9RSKvKx0op1Zl8K39pnijNpcuO-eatDNTIADOj2KKtPEp1cVfTsDUStKEQroGFx06_Kpj0WS9X68cJ3MnznqCl7xEwxz-yDeLiyCGYFhbxAer9-N

11. **New IETF Draft: Agent Public Key Infrastructure (APKI) for AI Agents**
    The `draft-sharif-apki-agent-pki-01` introduces an Agent Public Key Infrastructure (APKI) for certificate-based identity and trust for autonomous AI agents. This 18-page draft was submitted to the IETF on August 27, 2026.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGJkGh3vTH0FOIPSOMJ9RSKvKx0op1Zl8K39pnijNpcuO-eatDNTIADOj2KKtPEp1cVfTsDUStKEQroGFx06_Kpj0WS9X68cJ3MnznqCl7xEwxz-yDeLiyCGYFhbxAer9-N

12. **New IETF Draft: The Agent Record for AI Agent Identity and History**
    The `draft-maintainer-1f916-agent-record-00` describes an architecture for transparent, witness-countersigned event logs for AI agent identity, history, and memory. Submitted on August 12, 2026, it aims to provide verifiable identity continuity and integrity of an agent's claimed history without relying solely on the agent's operator or platform.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFuObtEvYDg5eO6xr9SHNb3DIqcQiZVukLePGhYmDUiHLuhQMQWyoXlK9Xucbt9S8T-EfA6_H8Ogt-xj-DBPcwLh9PJjybnFddDh9ODsd8T4IwI4aTOH37l9gkX-DpbWl9EDjedFDDYmbp19TktqO6M9_Aw30vLnnKQFuPd14yG

13. **W3C Publishes Decentralized Identifier Resolution (DID Resolution) v1 as Candidate Recommendation**
    On August 6, 2026, the W3C published Decentralized Identifier Resolution (DID Resolution) v1 as a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot, with a comment deadline of September 3, 2026. This is a significant step towards standardizing how Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) are resolved, which is foundational for verifiable AI agent identity.
    Source: https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEKV1dUBqoiuTCANlUk3-JH94lAnvOvbVKpt7J7pHQ7aJt3eB-Us-IM_scQJfRKdDMoLUiO4OvFehaksJyOjBgE-OGBH1C3UQyc5JANKXkrqUzt1FD9fT2mWjW8c4slZNIWxld1PPdpG8lHjL0KJmvKV4F-Pq1CKqJ7q45tx6AmU-KAmK9yKITdfdYP

2. [ietf.org](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-daniel-ai-agent-internet-architecture/)

Here's a compact digest of new or updated IETF drafts, W3C proposals, or standards-body activity on AI agent authentication, web bot auth, agents.txt, llms.txt, or agent identity from the last 30 days:

1.  **IETF Draft: AI Agent Authentication and Authorization (draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-01)**
    This Internet-Draft, updated on March 30, 2026, proposes a model for authenticating and authorizing AI agent interactions. It leverages existing standards like Workload Identity in Multi-System Environments (WIMSE) and OAuth 2.0, aiming to apply or extend them rather than define new protocols for agent identity and permissions.
    *   Authoritative Source: [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-klrc-aiagent-auth/01/](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-klrc-aiagent-auth/01/) (Note: The provided search result links to a Google redirect, but the IETF Datatracker is the primary source for drafts).

2.  **IETF Draft: Web Bot Auth for Cryptographic Agent Verification**
    Web Bot Auth is an IETF draft standard designed to enable cryptographic verification of AI agents. Each agent holds a private key, publishes its public key, and signs every HTTP request, allowing websites to cryptographically confirm the agent's identity. Google is actively experimenting with this protocol using the identity `https://agent.bot.goog`.
    *   Authoritative Source: While a direct IETF Datatracker link for "Web Bot Auth" wasn't explicitly provided in the snippets, the descriptions consistently refer to it as an IETF draft standard. The Google-Agent announcement and Cloudflare blog post serve as strong indicators of its active development and adoption.

3.  **W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group Activity on Agent Identity Models**
    The W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group is actively exploring and defining agent identity models as part of its mission to develop open, interoperable protocols for AI agents on the Web. A document titled "AI Agent Protocol Use Cases and Requirements" was published by this group on April 1, 2026, outlining the need for standardized authentication mechanisms for agents to mutually identify each other.
    *   Authoritative Source: [https://www.w3.org/community/aiagent/](https://www.w3.org/community/aiagent/) (W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group page) and [https://www.w3.org/community/aiagent/wiki/AI_Agent_Protocol_Use_Cases_and_Requirements](https://www.w3.org/community/aiagent/wiki/AI_Agent_Protocol_Use_Cases_and_Requirements) (for the specific document).

4.  **Emerging Web Standard: llms.txt for AI Content Guidance**
    `llms.txt` is an emerging web standard proposed to help large language models (LLMs) better navigate and understand website content. This plain text, markdown-formatted file, placed at the root of a domain, acts as a curated index to guide AI crawlers and systems to the most important pages, differing from `robots.txt` by providing guidance rather than access control.
    *   Authoritative Source: While not a formal IETF or W3C standard yet, its widespread discussion and adoption are noted in industry blogs. Cloudflare's blog and SiteSpeakAI provide detailed explanations.

5.  **W3C Web Standard: WebMCP (navigator.modelContext API) for AI Agent Interaction**
    WebMCP is a W3C web standard that enables websites to expose structured context, tools, and prompts to AI agents directly in the browser via the `navigator.modelContext` API. This allows AI agents to interact with a website's data and capabilities without requiring API keys or custom integrations. A Draft Community Group Report defining this API was published on February 10, 2026, with discussions and implementations continuing within the last 30 days.
    *   Authoritative Source: [https://www.w3.org/community/webmachinelearning/](https://www.w3.org/community/webmachinelearning/) (W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group page) and articles like Flyweel's provide context on its status.

6.  **NIST's Focus on AI Agent Identity and Human Approval Verification**
    The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is emphasizing the critical need for identity frameworks that link AI agent identity, human authenticity, and real-time risk signals to maintain trust in enterprise AI systems. Organizations like Pindrop and 1Password have submitted responses to NIST's concept paper, highlighting the challenges of continuous authentication and authorization for reasoning agents.
    *   Authoritative Source: Pindrop and 1Password blogs discuss their responses to NIST's concept paper, indicating active engagement with NIST's work in this area.

## Cited sources
1. [ietf.org](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-klrc-aiagent-auth/)
2. [nohacks.co](https://nohacks.co/blog/google-agent-user-agent)
3. [cloudflare.com](https://blog.cloudflare.com/agent-readiness/)
4. [w3.org](https://www.w3.org/community/reports/)
5. [github.io](https://w3c-cg.github.io/ai-agent-protocol/use_case.html)
6. [citeme.io](https://www.citeme.io/ressources/llms-txt-file-the-complete-guide-to-ai-seo-and-why-this-file-changes-everything-for-your-llms-strategy)
7. [sitespeak.ai](https://sitespeak.ai/blog/llms-txt-what-it-is-why-you-need-one)
8. [flyweel.co](https://www.flyweel.co/blog/what-is-webmcp)
9. [pindrop.com](https://www.pindrop.com/article/nist-reaction-ai-agents-need-identity-and-human-approval-needs-verification/)
10. [1password.com](https://1password.com/blog/agent-identity)
